angle: Unlike other L10 materials that compute tests, this video builds the null-hypothesis idea purely through repeated toy drug trials, contrasting confident rejection against failing to reject when replicates wobble only slightly.
angle_detail: Start with [09:55]–[12:43], where the narrator argues the only testable default is zero difference because any nonzero guess is arbitrary. Then watch [12:43]–[13:44] for the small-versus-large-sample intuition about when random wobble stops mattering. Note the notation gap: the video talks in drug A/B mean differences and never writes H0/H1, test statistics, or p-values, so pair it with a video that computes a test and skip the closing promo from [13:44] on.
